common_name: Abba Dabba Do Hosta (Gold-Margined Blue-Green Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Abba Dabba Do carries broad, rounded blue-green leaves rimmed with a wide, irregular gold-to-cream margin that widens and brightens as the season progresses, giving the clump a bolder two-toned look than more evenly variegated hostas. Pale lavender flowers rise on tall scapes above the foliage in mid to late summer. The vigorous, upright mound bulks up quickly for a variegated cultivar, making it a reliable focal point in a shaded bed within just a few growing seasons.

directions: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Baby Bunting forms a tight, slow-growing mound of small, rounded, blue-gray leaves with good substance for its size, giving it the thick-textured charm of larger blue hostas but scaled down for rock gardens, troughs, and path edges. Near-white to pale lavender flowers appear on short scapes in summer, rising just above the foliage. Because it stays diminutive for years, it rarely needs dividing and pairs well with miniature ferns and sedges in a shaded container planting.

common_name: Frosted Jade Hosta (Green Leaf White-Margined Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Frosted Jade produces large, glossy, deep green leaves edged in a wide, irregular creamy-white margin with gently undulating edges, giving the clump a crisp, frosted look that holds up well through summer heat. Pale lavender flowers appear on tall scapes in mid to late summer above the foliage. This vigorous, spreading cultivar makes an excellent large-scale groundcover or background planting in a woodland border, where its bold color contrast reads clearly against darker green companions.

common_name: Abiqua Recluse Hosta (Deeply Cupped Blue Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial to full shade. Like its Abiqua-line relatives, Abiqua Recluse produces thick, heavily corrugated, deep blue-green leaves that cup tightly inward, forming a dense, low mound with exceptional substance and slug resistance for a blue hosta. Near-white flowers appear on short, stout scapes mostly hidden within the foliage in early summer. The tight, rounded habit and rugose texture make it a striking specimen near a shaded path or water feature, though like other thick-substance blue hostas it is slow to bulk up and resents frequent division.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Blue Wedgewood forms a compact, symmetrical mound of smooth, powdery blue-gray leaves that hold their frosty color well into summer before gradually greening as the surface bloom wears away. Near-white flowers open on medium-height scapes in early summer, held just above the foliage. Its neat, well-proportioned size makes it useful as a repeating accent along a shaded border edge, where its cool color reads clearly against darker-leaved companions.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Stiletto is a narrow-leaved miniature hosta, its slender, lance-shaped dark green leaves edged in a crisp white margin that gives the small mound a fine, almost grass-like texture unusual among broader-leaved hostas. Lavender flowers rise on slender scapes above the foliage in summer. Its narrow leaf form and small stature make it a distinctive edging plant for a shaded path or the front of a mixed hosta collection, where wide-leaved cultivars would otherwise overwhelm it.

common_name: Northern Exposure Silver Heuchera (Silver-Leaved Villosa Hybrid Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring or fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade, providing afternoon shade protection in hot climates.

directions: Plant container-grown plants in spring or fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade, providing afternoon shade protection in hot climates. Bred from Heuchera villosa for heat and humidity tolerance, Northern Exposure Silver produces large, ruffled leaves with a bright silvery overlay set off by dark purple-black veining and undertones, a bolder and more heat-resistant take on the classic silver-leaf coral bells look. Airy sprays of small white flowers rise on wiry stems above the foliage in early summer, drawing bees and hummingbirds. Its large-leaved, vigorous habit and superior summer heat tolerance make it a sturdier choice than thinner-leaved silver heucheras for southern and humid gardens.

common_name: Stainless Steel Heuchera (Metallic Silver-Purple Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade.

directions: Plant container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade. Stainless Steel produces ruffled, metallic silver-gray leaves brushed with a subtle purple undertone and fine dark veining, giving the compact mound a cool, brushed-metal sheen distinct from the warmer amber and caramel tones of many other heuchera cultivars. Small white flowers appear on thin, wiry stems above the foliage in early summer. Its tidy, uniform habit and strong leaf color retention through summer heat make it a dependable edging or container plant where a cool silver tone is wanted against darker companions.
